mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate at or below 0.25% signals active monetary accommodation, reducing equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through lower cost of capital.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 10.0% indicates severe economic distress, triggering immediate risk-off sentiment that produces negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 10.0%, or the signal fails to outperform baseline returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer and business demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through earnings momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when both GDPC1 and HOUST show growth, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 85.0 indicates acute supply chain disruption, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days in supply shock regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 85.0, or the signal fails during documented supply shocks (e.g., 2008-2009).

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL monthly growth exceeding 0.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL growth rate > 0.5%, or the signal's Rank IC is negative over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth rate declining below -0.5% in 3 months indicates labor market contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth rate < -0.5%, or the signal does not correlate with historical labor market downturns.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) reflect strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through sustained earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when both RSAFS and HOUST show growth, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) increase discount rates and reduce liquidity, producing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days through heightened risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the signal fails during historical tightening periods (e.g., 1994, 2000).
